title: Agent-side capability handshake and cost hinting spec
author: Marisol Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines a lightweight, backward-compatible handshake between API clients (SDKs, gateways, and mobile/web agents) and Redwood inference endpoints to exchange:
- client capability advertisement (what features the client can accept and synthesize),
- server-side cost / fidelity hints (approx. token cost, estimated latency, fidelity tier), and
- runtime observability verbosity and sampling directives.

The goal is to make routing, fallback, and cost-aware client behavior deterministic and testable without coupling clients to internal runtime topology. This is a standards doc for the Redwood public/private inference APIs and is intended to be implemented by SDKs, edge-gateways, and the service mesh sidecars.

Background and motivation

Problem: clients currently make best-effort calls to the API and the server returns a response without a formal pre-call signal about expected cost/latency or accepted feature set. This leads to:
- client-side hedging/backoff mismatches,
- inaccurate cost estimates shown to end users, and
- inability for gateways to choose the appropriate model variant at the edge.

This handshake addresses those gaps by formalizing a small header and preflight exchange pattern that is:
1) opt-in (clients advertise capabilities),
2) incremental (server returns hints when available), and
3) safe (hints are advisory only and cannot be used to alter client resource quotas).

Specification summary

High level: clients MAY include capability headers on requests. The server MAY respond with advisory hint headers. When available, the server MAY also return a structured JSON `x-rw-handshake` payload in the response body on preflight endpoints.

Headers (primary)
- X-RW-Client-Capabilities: JSON-encoded, url-safe base64 of a compact capability object (see examples). Maximum header size: 1024 bytes.
- X-RW-Client-Intent: short token describing intent categories (chat|complete|embed|rerank|tool-call). Used by edge routing.
- X-RW-Request-Priority: integer 0..100 for tenant-supplied priority hint (optional; used for scheduling hints).

Advisory server headers (returned when applicable):
- X-RW-Cost-Estimate: approximate token cost in micro-units (string, e.g., "tokens=420;currency=micros")
- X-RW-Expected-Latency-ms: integer estimate of 90th percentile latency in ms for the current request signature
- X-RW-Fidelity-Tier: short label (high|balanced|low) indicating fallback fidelity the server selected to satisfy SLOs
- X-RW-Telemetry-Level: debug|verbose|standard|minimal (client may honor this to reduce local debug logging)

Preflight endpoint

To allow edge routers and heavy clients to make routing decisions without sending full payloads, the server exposes a preflight endpoint: POST /v1/handshake/preflight

- Request body: compact signature describing the request (model, seq_len_hint, features).
- Response body: JSON object `handshake` with fields: server_cost_hint, model_variant_recommendation, telemetry_directives, fallback_rules.

Example preflight request (JSON):
{
  "model": "rw-open-7b-v1",
  "prompt_signature": "sig:chat:avg-64"
}
